question: Which firmware LVGL timer veneers can safely drive page-owner incremental refresh?
prototype_hypothesis: lv_timer_create(callback, period_ms, user_data) returns a periodic LVGL timer whose callback receives the timer object; lv_timer_del(timer) synchronously removes that timer. Both calls must run in the LVGL/page-owner context.
callsite_evidence: sub_C588758 is a one-instruction Thumb veneer to 0x1C060035 and has more than 200 firmware callsites using r0=callback, r1=period, r2=user_data; sub_C49C32C calls it with sub_C49BDFC, 100 ms, and NULL, then retains the returned pointer
sub_C16CF3C is the recovered LVGL lv_timer_handler and invokes the callback stored in each timer with the timer object in r0, matching the standard LVGL timer callback ABI

sub_C587EF0 is a one-instruction Thumb veneer to 0x1C0600A9 and has hundreds of timer cleanup callsites; sub_C49BDFC and sub_C5F3748 pass their retained timer pointer in r0, call it, then clear the retained pointer
The recorder path sub_C5F273C creates a 120000 ms timer through sub_C588758 and sub_C5F3748 deletes the same retained timer through sub_C587EF0
control_flow_evidence: Creation returns an opaque timer pointer retained by the caller; callback execution is serialized by lv_timer_handler in the LVGL context
Deletion receives the retained pointer in r0; observed callers clear their ownership slot immediately after deletion
A native page may therefore create the timer during on_create, suppress work while paused, and delete it during on_destroy without allowing Bluetooth callbacks to touch LVX
ownership_analysis: The page backend exclusively owns one timer pointer per live page. The timer is created only after the first page render succeeds, remains valid across pause/resume, and is deleted before page widget pointers are cleared on destroy.
unsafe_assumptions: These are target-private LVGL veneers and must only be called after the exact firmware identity guard succeeds
Callbacks and delete must remain on the page/LVGL owner thread
The callback must not retain widget pointers beyond page destruction or delete the timer concurrently from another firmware context
recommended_probe: Open the Headphones page, leave it active through repeated discovery callbacks, pause/resume it, then open/close it 100 times while confirming automatic model updates, preserved scroll position, and no timer callback after on_destroy.

artifacts.role: LVGL timer handler and callback ABI
retained timer delete and clear callsite
